findings.body: The `imp` module was removed in Python 3.12. Importing it raises `ModuleNotFoundError` on any supported runtime, so `load()` will crash before it can do anything. Even on older Pythons, `imp.find_module`/`imp.load_module` are deprecated since 3.4 and slated for removal. findings.body: `imp.load_module(name, file, pathname, description)` takes four positional arguments after `name`. The code unpacks `imp.find_module(name)` (which yields a 3-tuple) into the remaining three slots, so the call shape is correct in count — but `imp.load_module` is documented to require the module to NOT already exist in `sys.modules`; if it does, ImportError is raised. More importantly, `imp.load_module` writes the loaded module into `sys.modules` as a side effect and returns it, but the function does not handle the case where `find_module` returns `None` (no module found), in which case unpacking raises TypeError.

findings.body: The range now uses `len(items) - 1` as the stop value. For a list of length n, `range(0, n-1, size)` yields indices 0, size, 2*size, ... up to the largest multiple of size strictly less than n-1. The final chunk (the one starting at the largest multiple of size that is < n) is never produced, so the last `size` items are silently dropped.
